1	# 0017. Eval harness runner
2	
3	**Date**: 2026-09-08
4	**Status**: Accepted
5	
6	## Summary
7	
8	This spec defines the one command that runs feature 15's sixteen ground truth pairs against the real scorer and reports which ones held up. Each pair is scored five times for real, since the scoring model's own randomness is not fixed, and a pair only counts as passing when a clear majority of those five runs land on the expected answer. Three kinds of pair need their own rule beyond a plain majority: a pair that measures instability on purpose, a trio of pairs that must stay consistent with each other, and a pair where too many runs failed outright to trust any answer at all. The command prints a table and writes a JSON report every time it runs, and it costs real money each time, so it lives behind its own explicit command rather than inside the free test suite.
9	
10	## Context
11	
12	See [rationale.md](rationale.md) for the full problem context, the options weighed for where and how this runs, and the rejected paths.
13	
14	## Requirements
15	
16	**User stories**:
17	- As the person maintaining the scoring rubric, I want one command that scores every ground truth pair for real and tells me which ones no longer match, so a prompt or model change is checked against real expectations rather than a fresh read of the output.
18	- As the person running this command, I want to iterate on one pair or one tag cheaply, so debugging a single failing pair does not spend the whole weekly allowance.
19	- As the person reading a report later, I want it to record which model and which rubric wording it was measured against, so a report from three weeks ago can tell "the scorer changed" apart from "the rubric changed".
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria**:
22	
23	- **AC-1**: One command (`pnpm eval`) runs every pair in feature 15's committed set and prints, for each pair, a pass, fail, or inconclusive verdict together with the actual band(s) observed. Before minting any session or spending any vendor call, a top level `beforeAll` runs `validateGroundTruth()` against the committed `ARCHETYPES` and `PAIRS`; if it returns any issue, the run throws with every issue printed, one per line, and exits non zero. This check runs even under a `-t` filtered invocation (AC-8), since a `beforeAll` is not itself filtered out the way an `it` would be.
24	- **AC-2**: Every pair is scored through the real `scoreListing()` path, passing the run's one minted fixture session (`session.jar`) as its `cookieAdapter` argument, exactly the shape `test/integration/fit-scoring-live.test.ts` already uses. One session is minted once for the whole run (not once per pair), reused by every call. A pair's five reruns happen one after another inside that pair's own test body (never fired at once), because they exist to measure how much the same input moves between separate calls; different pairs' test bodies may run at the same time as each other, bounded by an explicit concurrency limit (Build plan, step 1).
25	- **AC-3**: `scoreListing()` can return three kinds of outcome, and each is handled differently:
26	  - **A usage gate refusal** (`Result` success carrying `allowed: false`, any of the five `UsageGateReason` values) is never counted toward any pair's denominator. The FIRST refusal seen anywhere in the run aborts the entire run immediately: every other pair's in flight or not yet started test fails with the refusal's own reason named, the partial report is still written (marked `aborted: "<reason>"`, carrying whatever pair verdicts had already completed), and the run exits non zero. A budget or kill switch stop is an operator condition, not evidence about the rubric, and must never be read as sixteen ordinary `inconclusive` verdicts.
27	  - **A rerun failure** (a `Result` failure: a vendor timeout or a malformed response) counts against that one pair's own denominator only and never aborts the run.
28	  - **A scored success** (`allowed: true`, a real band) is what the verdict rule below counts.
29	
30	  A pair's verdict needs at least 3 of its 5 reruns to be scored successes; with fewer than 3, the pair is `inconclusive` (sub reason `insufficient-successes`), reporting whatever successes did land, never silently folded into a pass or a fail. With 3 or more successes, and the pair is not tagged `stability-probe` (AC-4 covers that case separately): compute how many of the successes landed on each band. If one band holds a strict majority (more than half of the successes), that is the pair's verdict band, and the pair passes if that band equals `expectedBand`, or, when `acceptableBands` is present, if it is one of them. If no band holds a strict majority (e.g. a 2 and 2 split out of 4 successes, or a 1, 1, 1 split out of 3), the pair is `inconclusive` (sub reason `no-majority`) UNLESS `acceptableBands` is present and every successful rerun's band is inside it, in which case the pair passes with no single verdict band, reporting the full observed split instead (this is what makes `boundary-seniority-gap`'s own honest, anchor stated ambiguity, e.g. a 2 and 2 `weak_match`/`not_a_match` split, a pass rather than a false `inconclusive`).
31	- **AC-4**: A pair tagged `stability-probe` is judged differently, but only once AC-3's own 3 of 5 successes floor is met (fewer than 3 successes is still `inconclusive` under AC-3, unchanged). With 3 or more successes, `expectedBand` is not consulted and no majority is computed: the pair passes only if every one of its successful reruns' band is inside `acceptableBands`. One success landing outside that set fails the pair even if every other success matched, since this pair's whole point is that no single run should be trusted as the answer. Because there may be no single winning band, this pair's verdict is always reported as its observed distribution (e.g. `{ strong_match: 3, possible_match: 2 }`), never a lone band.
32	- **AC-5**: The three `preference-isolation` tagged pairs (`preference-match`, `preference-violation`, `preference-title-conflict`) are each judged individually by AC-3 first, exactly like any other pair, with no special treatment of their own verdicts. Once all three have a verdict that is neither `inconclusive` nor missing (skipped by a `-t` filter that excluded one of them, in which case the check below is skipped and reported as `leak-check-skipped`), the run additionally compares `preference-match`'s verdict band against `preference-violation`'s and against `preference-title-conflict`'s:
33	  - If `preference-match`'s band equals both conflict pairs' bands, nothing further is reported; each pair's own individual pass or fail already stands.
34	  - If all three bands equal each other but none of them equals `strong_match` (`expectedBand`), the run reports `baseline-drift`: something moved the band for every pairing equally, which is a rubric or model question, not a leak, since nothing about the conflicting posting text distinguished itself.
35	  - If `preference-match`'s band differs from either conflict pair's band, the run reports `preference-leak-suspected`, distinctly from an ordinary mismatch: the skill and experience content is identical across all three, so a divergence here can only be explained by the preference text that does differ between them.
36	- **AC-6**: Every printed and reported verdict names its own denominator (e.g. "good_match, 3 of 3 succeeded" or, for a distribution shaped verdict, "3 strong_match / 2 possible_match, 5 of 5 succeeded"), never just a band on its own, so a reader can tell a verdict resting on the minimum 3 successes apart from one resting on all 5, and can see a split even where the pair still passed.
37	- **AC-7**: The command's own exit code is non zero if any pair fails, any pair is `inconclusive`, a preference leak is reported, or the run aborted on a usage gate refusal (AC-3); zero only when every pair that ran passed cleanly and nothing aborted.
38	- **AC-8**: A subset of pairs can be run without spending calls on the rest of the set, by reusing the test runner's own name filter against each pair's test name, which is generated as `` `${pair.id} [${pair.tags.join(" ")}]` `` (e.g. `control-direct-match [control]`, `stability-probe-generic [stability-probe]`), so `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` matches one pair by id and `pnpm eval -t stability-probe` matches every pair carrying that tag. A filtered run still writes a JSON report; it records which filter produced it and lists every pair that did not run as `skipped`, never silently absent. Filters can overlap (e.g. `-t control` also matches every pair whose id happens to start with `control-`); this is an accepted property of substring matching, not a bug to design around.
39	- **AC-9**: The command writes a JSON report every run, in addition to the console table, to a directory this repository does not track, at `test/eval/.output/<ISO timestamp with colons replaced by dashes>.json`, creating that directory if it does not exist. Each report is a single `EvalReport` object (defined in `test/eval/report.ts`) recording: the filter used (if any) and every skipped pair id; per pair, its status (`pass`/`fail`/`inconclusive`), sub reason where relevant, denominator, and every observed band (or band distribution); the preference leak check's own outcome; the run's overall status and aborted reason if any; and, once per report, which model answered (via the shared `resolvedModel()` guard on `TIERS.ai_scoring.model`, never a name typed into the harness) and a hash of `BAND_ANCHORS`'s current text (`bandAnchorsHash()`, defined once and shared with the AC-10 test, so "the same way" is true by construction rather than by two separate implementations agreeing).
40	- **AC-10**: A committed test (no vendor call, runs under the ordinary free unit suite) asserts `BAND_ANCHORS` literally equals today's text (`toEqual` against the five strings written inline in the test, never a snapshot file, which a routine `vitest -u` could silently rewrite) and that `bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS)` equals today's computed hash, both failing by name and naming spec 0016's dataset, the moment either changes, so a rubric edit is caught at commit time rather than only by a human comparing two JSON reports later.
41	- **AC-11**: The command works against a changed model with no code edit to this feature: nothing here names a vendor or a model id directly, every call goes through the existing `scoreListing()` / `TIERS` path exactly as the rest of the app does, and the model id reported (AC-9) is read off that same resolved config.
42	
43	## Options considered
44	
45	See [rationale.md](rationale.md).
46	
47	## Decision
48	
49	**Chosen option**: Option 3, a dedicated `eval` Vitest project under `test/eval/`, run only through its own explicit `pnpm eval` command, never swept into `pnpm test` or `pnpm test:integration` (rationale.md has the full comparison against a plain script and against folding this into the existing `integration-serial` project).
50	
51	## Rationale
52	
53	Full reasoning and the rejected options: see [rationale.md](rationale.md).
54	
55	## Feature design
56	
57	**Data model sketch**: none new. This feature reads feature 15's already committed `ARCHETYPES` and `PAIRS` (`src/features/scoring/eval/`) and writes only to a gitignored local file; no table, no migration.
58	
59	**State transitions**: none, a script run start to finish. Per pair verdict states: `pass` · `fail` · `inconclusive` (sub reasons `insufficient-successes`, `no-majority`). Run level states: `completed` · `aborted` (carrying a `UsageGateReason`).
60	
61	**API surface**: not a request surface. The one "endpoint" is the command line:
62	
63	| Command | Key inputs | Key outputs | Auth | Key errors |
64	|---|---|---|---|---|
65	| `pnpm eval` | optional `-t <pattern>`, matched against each pair's generated test name (id and tags, AC-8) | console table, `test/eval/.output/<timestamp>.json`, an exit code | one fixture session minted once for the run (`test/helpers/mintFixtureUser`, `test/helpers/mintSession`), reused by every call | `validateGroundTruth()` finding an issue in the committed data (AC-1, refused before any spend); a usage gate refusal aborting the run (AC-3); a vendor timeout or malformed response on one rerun (counted against that pair's own denominator, AC-3); the local Supabase stack not running (the existing `require-stack` global setup's own named failure) |
66	
67	**Value sourcing**:
68	| Action | Value produced / displayed | Source |
69	|---|---|---|
70	| Scoring one rerun of one pair | which profile and listing are sent | `pair.listing` and `ARCHETYPES.find(a => a.id === pair.archetypeId).profile`, exactly feature 15's committed data (AC-1) |
71	| Scoring one rerun of one pair | the caller's identity | the one fixture session minted once in this run's own setup, passed as `scoreListing()`'s `cookieAdapter` argument, reused (not reminted) across every pair and rerun (AC-2) |
72	| Computing a pair's verdict | the pass, fail, or inconclusive call, and any sub reason | the pure verdict function in `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts`, given the pair's `expectedBand`, `acceptableBands`, and `tags`, and this run's own array of scored/failed/refused rerun outcomes, per the rule in AC-3 and AC-4 |
73	| Computing the preference leak flag | `preference-leak-suspected` · `baseline-drift` · nothing · `leak-check-skipped` | the three `preference-isolation` pairs' own verdict bands, already computed by the step above, compared per AC-5 |
74	| The JSON report's model field | which model answered | `resolvedModel(TIERS.ai_scoring.model).modelId`, `resolvedModel` exported from `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts` (lifted from the equivalent guard already written, but kept private, in `src/lib/ai/tiers.test.ts:23-30`), never a name typed into the harness (AC-9, AC-11) |
75	| The JSON report's anchors field | whether the rubric text has moved since the data was authored | `bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS)`, a pure function in `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors-hash.ts` (sha256 over `BANDS.map(b => \`${b}:${BAND_ANCHORS[b]}\`).join("\n")`, first 12 hex characters), imported by both this report writer and the AC-10 test, so both read the one real function (AC-9) |
76	| The run's own exit code | pass, fail, aborted, or a mix | the aggregate of every pair's verdict, the preference leak flag, and whether the run aborted on a usage gate refusal (AC-7) |
77	
78	**Key invariants**:
79	- A pair's five reruns are never fired concurrently with each other; only different pairs' test bodies may overlap (AC-2), bounded by `maxConcurrency` (Build plan, step 1).
80	- A verdict is never printed or reported without its denominator alongside it (AC-6).
81	- `pnpm eval` is never reachable from `pnpm test` or `pnpm test:integration`: it is its own Vitest project, selected only by explicit `--project eval` (which the `pnpm eval` script wraps), so no existing command starts spending real vendor calls by accident.
82	- Nothing under `test/eval/` or `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts` names a vendor package or a model id; every real call goes through `scoreListing()`, and the reported model id goes through the shared `resolvedModel()` guard (AC-11).
83	- The `BAND_ANCHORS` drift assertions (AC-10) live in the ordinary unit suite (`pnpm test`), never behind a vendor call, so a rubric edit is caught on every push, not only when someone happens to run the harness.
84	- The minted fixture user is deleted (`deleteFixtureUser`) after the report is written, in an `afterAll`, matching `test/helpers/fixture-user.ts`'s own reason for existing: an undeleted fixture user otherwise accumulates in the local database on every run, the same way `fit-scoring-live.test.ts` already avoids it. Cleanup runs after the report write, in that order, so a cleanup failure can never destroy the run's own output.
85	- One session is expected to outlive the whole run (sixteen pairs, bounded concurrency, five sequential calls each): this is assumed to comfortably fit inside Supabase's session lifetime today, and is not re verified per call. If feature 15's set grows large enough, or `ai_scoring` itself grows slower, to approach that lifetime, this assumption needs revisiting (Follow up).
86	
87	**Security model**: No user facing surface and no user data. The fixture session this feature mints is the same development only, `DEV_SESSION_ENABLED` gated path `test/helpers/session.ts` and `test/helpers/fixture-user.ts` already use for `fit-scoring-live.test.ts`; nothing new is added to that gate. The one real exposure is that every archetype's `summary`, `skills`, and `experience` text reaches OpenAI on every run of this command, which is exactly spec 0016's own AC-1 (no real person, no real employer) doing its job here too.
88	
89	**Configuration required**: none new. Reuses `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, and `DEV_SESSION_ENABLED`, already validated by `src/env.ts` and already required for the local Supabase stack this command needs running.
90	
91	**Critical test scenarios**:
92	- Happy path: `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` scores that one pair for real, five sequential reruns under the one minted session, and prints a passing verdict with its denominator (e.g. "strong_match, 5 of 5 succeeded"), verifies **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-6**, **AC-9**.
93	- Failure case: a pair whose five reruns come back as 2 scored and 3 vendor failures is reported `inconclusive` (`insufficient-successes`) rather than a false pass or fail, the run's own exit code is non zero, and the other pairs in the same run still complete, verifies **AC-3**, **AC-7**.
94	- Abort case: constructed against `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts`'s own fixtures, the first rerun outcome carrying `allowed: false` (any `UsageGateReason`) stops the run from counting it toward any denominator and marks the run `aborted`, verifies **AC-3**.
95	- Data quality gate: `validateGroundTruth()` returning even one issue against a deliberately broken fixture set stops the command before any vendor call is made, verifies **AC-1**.
96	- Cross pair check: constructed verdicts where `preference-match` lands on `strong_match` but `preference-violation` lands on `good_match` (with `preference-title-conflict` unchanged) trip `preference-leak-suspected`, while all three landing together on `good_match` instead trips `baseline-drift`, verified against `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts`'s own fixtures rather than a real run, verifies **AC-5**.
97	- Drift guard: editing `BAND_ANCHORS`'s text fails the AC-10 test by name, under the ordinary free `pnpm test`, verifies **AC-10**.
98	
99	## Build plan
100	
101	This project's default build approach is Tracer Bullet (a thin end to end slice proven before scaling). Applied here: prove the whole real path, real vendor call, real verdict, real report, on exactly one pair before scaling to all sixteen and the cross pair and aggregate logic.
102	
103	1. Add the `eval` Vitest project to `vitest.config.mts`: `extends: true` (pulls in the root `resolve.tsconfigPaths` and the `server-only` alias every other project already relies on; omitting it is exactly the failure Option 2 was rejected for, since `scoreListing()`'s own `import "server-only"` throws without it), `include: ["test/eval/**/*.test.ts"]`, `environment: "node"`, the shared `setupFiles`, `globalSetup: ["./test/setup/require-stack.ts"]`, `testTimeout: 300_000` (five sequential `ai_scoring` calls at its own 30 second `timeoutMs` ceiling each, plus headroom, since one pair's test body cannot finish faster than its slowest rerun), `hookTimeout: 60_000` (the fixture user mint against a possibly cold stack), `maxConcurrency: 4` (a real, installed Vitest 4.1.11 option bounding how many pairs' test bodies run at once; set explicitly rather than left at whatever the installed version currently defaults to), and `fileParallelism: false` scoped to this project alone, the same reason `integration-serial` already carries it: this project is written to hold exactly one file sharing one minted session and one report writer, and a second file here would run in a separate worker by Vitest's own default, mint a second session, and race the first on the same report filename. Add the `"eval": "vitest run --project eval"` script to `package.json`. Satisfies **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-11**.
104	2. Export `resolvedModel()` from `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts` (lifted from the equivalent already written, but currently private to `src/lib/ai/tiers.test.ts`, which switches to importing it instead of keeping its own copy), and add `bandAnchorsHash()` as a small pure function in `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors-hash.ts`. Write the pure verdict logic in `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts`: the three way outcome classification (refusal, rerun failure, scored success) from AC-3, the majority vote with the 3 of 5 inconclusive floor and the no majority/`acceptableBands` exception, the distinct `stability-probe` "every success inside `acceptableBands`" rule (AC-4), and the `preference-isolation` baseline comparison (AC-5). Wire `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts` against constructed fixtures for each rule, no vendor call involved. Satisfies **AC-3**, **AC-4**, **AC-5**, **AC-6**.
105	3. The thin thread: `test/eval/harness.test.ts`, one `describe("eval harness")`, a top level `beforeAll` running `validateGroundTruth()` (throwing with every issue if any, before anything else) then minting the one fixture session for the run; one `it.concurrent` per pair named `` `${pair.id} [${pair.tags.join(" ")}]` ``, whose body awaits five sequential `scoreListing()` calls, feeds the outcomes to step 2's verdict function, stores the result in a module scoped `Map<string, PairVerdict>` keyed by pair id, and asserts (via the test context's own `expect`, required under `it.concurrent`) that the verdict's status is `pass`, so `fail` and `inconclusive` both fail their own test with the denominator and distribution in the message; and a final `afterAll` that runs the preference leak check against the map, writes the JSON report (including the model id and anchors hash), then deletes the fixture user. Prove this against exactly `control-direct-match` (real vendor calls) before scaling: get `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` green end to end. Satisfies the first slice of **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-9**.
106	4. Scale to the full sixteen pairs, confirm `maxConcurrency` and `fileParallelism` behave as designed under a real, unfiltered `pnpm eval` run, and confirm the run's own exit code is non zero on a fail, an inconclusive pair, a leak, or an abort, and zero only when everything that ran passed cleanly. Satisfies the rest of **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-7**, **AC-8**.
107	5. Add the committed `BAND_ANCHORS` drift test under `src/features/scoring/eval/` (the ordinary unit project, no vendor call): a literal `toEqual` pin of today's text plus a `bandAnchorsHash()` equality check, both failing by name, pointing at spec 0016's dataset, the moment either changes. Satisfies **AC-10**.
108	6. Add `/test/eval/.output/` to `.gitignore`. Satisfies **AC-9**.
109	
110	## Consequences
111	
112	**Positive**:
113	- Spec 0015's AC-2 (do the five bands actually spread real listings) and spec 0016's whole purpose (a ground truth set with nothing to run it against) both get their first real answer.
114	- The preference isolation check gives a structural, named way to catch a preference leaking into the band, distinct from an equally real but different finding (the rubric drifting for everyone at once), which closes the gap `rubric.ts`'s own comment names as otherwise untestable.
115	- The `BAND_ANCHORS` drift test means a rubric wording change is caught by the free, always run unit suite, not only by someone remembering to run the paid harness and compare two reports by hand.
116	- Reusing `scoreListing()` unchanged, rather than a second call path straight to `TIERS`, means this feature can never drift from what the real app actually sends; a schema or prompt change is proven here exactly as it is proven in production. Aborting the whole run on the first usage gate refusal, rather than absorbing it into ordinary per pair accounting, keeps that same honesty: a budget or kill switch stop is reported as exactly what it is, not laundered into a wall of `inconclusive` verdicts that would misdescribe what actually happened.
117	
118	**Negative / tradeoffs**:
119	- A full run spends 80 real vendor calls (16 pairs times 5 reruns) every time it runs the whole set; the `-t` subset filter is what keeps day to day iteration cheap, but this is still the largest deliberate, repeatable spend in this project, and it grows linearly with every future pair added to feature 15's set.
120	- The 3 of 5 success threshold for `inconclusive` means a genuinely bad but real result (all 5 reruns land on the same, wrong band) is never confused with a run too broken to trust, which is correct, but it also means an unlucky run (3 vendor timeouts and 2 real, matching answers) is reported exactly the same way as one with no useful data at all, even though 2 real matching answers is weak but real evidence. This spec accepts that loss rather than inventing a second, softer verdict tier.
121	- The preference leak check only covers the three pairs feature 15 built for exactly this purpose; it is not a general "did any preference move any band" detector across the other thirteen pairs, none of which vary a preference at all.
122	- `maxConcurrency` bounds how many pairs run at once, not how many vendor calls run at once across pairs; a pair whose own five reruns are mid flight does not free a concurrency slot until all five finish, so the actual number of simultaneous vendor calls can briefly exceed the pair level bound. This is accepted rather than built around, since the global day cap (1320) has wide headroom under this feature's whole weekly spend.
123	- Aborting the entire run on the first usage gate refusal means one unlucky global cap hit (shared with whatever else is calling `ai_scoring` at the time, including local `pnpm dev` usage) discards every result computed so far in that run, even pairs that had already cleanly passed. This is accepted because a refusal genuinely means the run's remaining data would not reflect real scoring anyway, not because the discarded cost is small.
124	
125	**Neutral**:
126	- If the ground truth set (feature 15) grows past sixteen pairs, this feature's cost and run time grow with it; nothing here caps the set's size, that boundary belongs to spec 0016.
127	- The JSON report format is not versioned or schema checked; it is a plain, structural artifact for a human to read or diff by hand, not a contract another program depends on. If that changes later (a dashboard, a CI gate reading these reports), the format becomes its own decision.
128	
129	## Follow-up
130	
131	- [ ] This spec deliberately does not gate `pnpm eval` behind an explicit opt-in environment variable the way `TEST_LIVE_MODEL_CALLS_ENABLED` gates the one paid case inside `pnpm test:integration`. The safety mechanism here is that `eval` is its own Vitest project, reachable only by naming `--project eval` explicitly, and never included in `pnpm test` or `pnpm test:integration`. If a later command is ever added that runs every Vitest project unfiltered, revisit whether that alone is still enough.
132	- [ ] The global day cap for `ai_scoring` (1320, shared across everything that calls this tier, including local `pnpm dev` usage on `/search`, not scoped per fixture user) is the real ceiling this feature can hit, not the account weekly cap (500): since this feature mints a fresh fixture user every run, that account counter starts at zero each time and is not the binding constraint. Roughly sixteen full 80 call runs a day share that global ceiling with everything else touching `ai_scoring` locally; worth watching once this ships if iteration gets heavy, not solved here.
133	- [ ] `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts`'s `TIERS[tier].model` is typed `LanguageModel`, a union that also permits a plain gateway model id string `tiers.ts` itself never constructs; the `resolvedModel()` guard this feature exports narrows past that, matching the reasoning already written beside the guard it replaces in `tiers.test.ts`. If `tiers.ts` ever legitimately needs the string form, `resolvedModel()`'s own throw is where that would first surface, and it would need revisiting then, not guessed at now.
134	- [x] Root `AGENTS.md`'s `## Commands` section (line 37) still describes Vitest as "two projects"; it was already stale before this feature (spec 0011 added the third, `integration-serial`, on 2026-09-03) and this feature adds a fourth plus a new `pnpm eval` script the commands list does not yet name. `/architect` does not edit `AGENTS.md`; flagging it here for `/sync` or a direct edit once this feature builds. **Done 2026-09-08 at feature close**, by direct edit, the option this item itself names. The claim was verified first and was accurate on both counts. The section now names all four projects with the spec that added each, and the commands block carries `pnpm eval` marked as paid, together with the fact that the binding ceiling is the shared `ai_scoring` global day cap rather than the account weekly cap, since the harness mints a fresh fixture user every run.
135	- [ ] This spec assumes the one minted session comfortably outlives a full run (sixteen pairs, bounded concurrency, five sequential calls each) without needing a refresh. If feature 15's set grows large enough, or a slower model tier is ever routed through this same harness, to make that assumption doubtful, re minting per pair (at the cost of more setup calls) is the fix, not something this build needs to solve preemptively.
136

# 0017. Eval harness runner

**Date**: 2026-09-08
**Status**: Accepted

## Summary

This spec defines the one command that runs feature 15's sixteen ground truth pairs against the real scorer and reports which ones held up. Each pair is scored five times for real, since the scoring model's own randomness is not fixed, and a pair only counts as passing when a clear majority of those five runs land on the expected answer. Three kinds of pair need their own rule beyond a plain majority: a pair that measures instability on purpose, a trio of pairs that must stay consistent with each other, and a pair where too many runs failed outright to trust any answer at all. The command prints a table and writes a JSON report every time it runs, and it costs real money each time, so it lives behind its own explicit command rather than inside the free test suite.

## Context

See [rationale.md](rationale.md) for the full problem context, the options weighed for where and how this runs, and the rejected paths.

## Requirements

**User stories**:
- As the person maintaining the scoring rubric, I want one command that scores every ground truth pair for real and tells me which ones no longer match, so a prompt or model change is checked against real expectations rather than a fresh read of the output.
- As the person running this command, I want to iterate on one pair or one tag cheaply, so debugging a single failing pair does not spend the whole weekly allowance.
- As the person reading a report later, I want it to record which model and which rubric wording it was measured against, so a report from three weeks ago can tell "the scorer changed" apart from "the rubric changed".

**Acceptance criteria**:

- **AC-1**: One command (`pnpm eval`) runs every pair in feature 15's committed set and prints, for each pair, a pass, fail, or inconclusive verdict together with the actual band(s) observed. Before minting any session or spending any vendor call, a top level `beforeAll` runs `validateGroundTruth()` against the committed `ARCHETYPES` and `PAIRS`; if it returns any issue, the run throws with every issue printed, one per line, and exits non zero. This check runs even under a `-t` filtered invocation (AC-8), since a `beforeAll` is not itself filtered out the way an `it` would be.
- **AC-2**: Every pair is scored through the real `scoreListing()` path, passing the run's one minted fixture session (`session.jar`) as its `cookieAdapter` argument, exactly the shape `test/integration/fit-scoring-live.test.ts` already uses. One session is minted once for the whole run (not once per pair), reused by every call. A pair's five reruns happen one after another inside that pair's own test body (never fired at once), because they exist to measure how much the same input moves between separate calls; different pairs' test bodies may run at the same time as each other, bounded by an explicit concurrency limit (Build plan, step 1).
- **AC-3**: `scoreListing()` can return three kinds of outcome, and each is handled differently:
  - **A usage gate refusal** (`Result` success carrying `allowed: false`, any of the five `UsageGateReason` values) is never counted toward any pair's denominator. The FIRST refusal seen anywhere in the run aborts the entire run immediately: every other pair's in flight or not yet started test fails with the refusal's own reason named, the partial report is still written (marked `aborted: "<reason>"`, carrying whatever pair verdicts had already completed), and the run exits non zero. A budget or kill switch stop is an operator condition, not evidence about the rubric, and must never be read as sixteen ordinary `inconclusive` verdicts.
  - **A rerun failure** (a `Result` failure: a vendor timeout or a malformed response) counts against that one pair's own denominator only and never aborts the run.
  - **A scored success** (`allowed: true`, a real band) is what the verdict rule below counts.

  A pair's verdict needs at least 3 of its 5 reruns to be scored successes; with fewer than 3, the pair is `inconclusive` (sub reason `insufficient-successes`), reporting whatever successes did land, never silently folded into a pass or a fail. With 3 or more successes, and the pair is not tagged `stability-probe` (AC-4 covers that case separately): compute how many of the successes landed on each band. If one band holds a strict majority (more than half of the successes), that is the pair's verdict band, and the pair passes if that band equals `expectedBand`, or, when `acceptableBands` is present, if it is one of them. If no band holds a strict majority (e.g. a 2 and 2 split out of 4 successes, or a 1, 1, 1 split out of 3), the pair is `inconclusive` (sub reason `no-majority`) UNLESS `acceptableBands` is present and every successful rerun's band is inside it, in which case the pair passes with no single verdict band, reporting the full observed split instead (this is what makes `boundary-seniority-gap`'s own honest, anchor stated ambiguity, e.g. a 2 and 2 `weak_match`/`not_a_match` split, a pass rather than a false `inconclusive`).
- **AC-4**: A pair tagged `stability-probe` is judged differently, but only once AC-3's own 3 of 5 successes floor is met (fewer than 3 successes is still `inconclusive` under AC-3, unchanged). With 3 or more successes, `expectedBand` is not consulted and no majority is computed: the pair passes only if every one of its successful reruns' band is inside `acceptableBands`. One success landing outside that set fails the pair even if every other success matched, since this pair's whole point is that no single run should be trusted as the answer. Because there may be no single winning band, this pair's verdict is always reported as its observed distribution (e.g. `{ strong_match: 3, possible_match: 2 }`), never a lone band.
- **AC-5**: The three `preference-isolation` tagged pairs (`preference-match`, `preference-violation`, `preference-title-conflict`) are each judged individually by AC-3 first, exactly like any other pair, with no special treatment of their own verdicts. Once all three have a verdict that is neither `inconclusive` nor missing (skipped by a `-t` filter that excluded one of them, in which case the check below is skipped and reported as `leak-check-skipped`), the run additionally compares `preference-match`'s verdict band against `preference-violation`'s and against `preference-title-conflict`'s:
  - If `preference-match`'s band equals both conflict pairs' bands, nothing further is reported; each pair's own individual pass or fail already stands.
  - If all three bands equal each other but none of them equals `strong_match` (`expectedBand`), the run reports `baseline-drift`: something moved the band for every pairing equally, which is a rubric or model question, not a leak, since nothing about the conflicting posting text distinguished itself.
  - If `preference-match`'s band differs from either conflict pair's band, the run reports `preference-leak-suspected`, distinctly from an ordinary mismatch: the skill and experience content is identical across all three, so a divergence here can only be explained by the preference text that does differ between them.
- **AC-6**: Every printed and reported verdict names its own denominator (e.g. "good_match, 3 of 3 succeeded" or, for a distribution shaped verdict, "3 strong_match / 2 possible_match, 5 of 5 succeeded"), never just a band on its own, so a reader can tell a verdict resting on the minimum 3 successes apart from one resting on all 5, and can see a split even where the pair still passed.
- **AC-7**: The command's own exit code is non zero if any pair fails, any pair is `inconclusive`, a preference leak is reported, or the run aborted on a usage gate refusal (AC-3); zero only when every pair that ran passed cleanly and nothing aborted.
- **AC-8**: A subset of pairs can be run without spending calls on the rest of the set, by reusing the test runner's own name filter against each pair's test name, which is generated as `` `${pair.id} [${pair.tags.join(" ")}]` `` (e.g. `control-direct-match [control]`, `stability-probe-generic [stability-probe]`), so `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` matches one pair by id and `pnpm eval -t stability-probe` matches every pair carrying that tag. A filtered run still writes a JSON report; it records which filter produced it and lists every pair that did not run as `skipped`, never silently absent. Filters can overlap (e.g. `-t control` also matches every pair whose id happens to start with `control-`); this is an accepted property of substring matching, not a bug to design around.
- **AC-9**: The command writes a JSON report every run, in addition to the console table, to a directory this repository does not track, at `test/eval/.output/<ISO timestamp with colons replaced by dashes>.json`, creating that directory if it does not exist. Each report is a single `EvalReport` object (defined in `test/eval/report.ts`) recording: the filter used (if any) and every skipped pair id; per pair, its status (`pass`/`fail`/`inconclusive`), sub reason where relevant, denominator, and every observed band (or band distribution); the preference leak check's own outcome; the run's overall status and aborted reason if any; and, once per report, which model answered (via the shared `resolvedModel()` guard on `TIERS.ai_scoring.model`, never a name typed into the harness) and a hash of `BAND_ANCHORS`'s current text (`bandAnchorsHash()`, defined once and shared with the AC-10 test, so "the same way" is true by construction rather than by two separate implementations agreeing).
- **AC-10**: A committed test (no vendor call, runs under the ordinary free unit suite) asserts `BAND_ANCHORS` literally equals today's text (`toEqual` against the five strings written inline in the test, never a snapshot file, which a routine `vitest -u` could silently rewrite) and that `bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS)` equals today's computed hash, both failing by name and naming spec 0016's dataset, the moment either changes, so a rubric edit is caught at commit time rather than only by a human comparing two JSON reports later.
- **AC-11**: The command works against a changed model with no code edit to this feature: nothing here names a vendor or a model id directly, every call goes through the existing `scoreListing()` / `TIERS` path exactly as the rest of the app does, and the model id reported (AC-9) is read off that same resolved config.

## Options considered

See [rationale.md](rationale.md).

## Decision

**Chosen option**: Option 3, a dedicated `eval` Vitest project under `test/eval/`, run only through its own explicit `pnpm eval` command, never swept into `pnpm test` or `pnpm test:integration` (rationale.md has the full comparison against a plain script and against folding this into the existing `integration-serial` project).

## Rationale

Full reasoning and the rejected options: see [rationale.md](rationale.md).

## Feature design

**Data model sketch**: none new. This feature reads feature 15's already committed `ARCHETYPES` and `PAIRS` (`src/features/scoring/eval/`) and writes only to a gitignored local file; no table, no migration.

**State transitions**: none, a script run start to finish. Per pair verdict states: `pass` · `fail` · `inconclusive` (sub reasons `insufficient-successes`, `no-majority`). Run level states: `completed` · `aborted` (carrying a `UsageGateReason`).

**API surface**: not a request surface. The one "endpoint" is the command line:

| Command | Key inputs | Key outputs | Auth | Key errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pnpm eval` | optional `-t <pattern>`, matched against each pair's generated test name (id and tags, AC-8) | console table, `test/eval/.output/<timestamp>.json`, an exit code | one fixture session minted once for the run (`test/helpers/mintFixtureUser`, `test/helpers/mintSession`), reused by every call | `validateGroundTruth()` finding an issue in the committed data (AC-1, refused before any spend); a usage gate refusal aborting the run (AC-3); a vendor timeout or malformed response on one rerun (counted against that pair's own denominator, AC-3); the local Supabase stack not running (the existing `require-stack` global setup's own named failure) |

**Value sourcing**:
| Action | Value produced / displayed | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Scoring one rerun of one pair | which profile and listing are sent | `pair.listing` and `ARCHETYPES.find(a => a.id === pair.archetypeId).profile`, exactly feature 15's committed data (AC-1) |
| Scoring one rerun of one pair | the caller's identity | the one fixture session minted once in this run's own setup, passed as `scoreListing()`'s `cookieAdapter` argument, reused (not reminted) across every pair and rerun (AC-2) |
| Computing a pair's verdict | the pass, fail, or inconclusive call, and any sub reason | the pure verdict function in `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts`, given the pair's `expectedBand`, `acceptableBands`, and `tags`, and this run's own array of scored/failed/refused rerun outcomes, per the rule in AC-3 and AC-4 |
| Computing the preference leak flag | `preference-leak-suspected` · `baseline-drift` · nothing · `leak-check-skipped` | the three `preference-isolation` pairs' own verdict bands, already computed by the step above, compared per AC-5 |
| The JSON report's model field | which model answered | `resolvedModel(TIERS.ai_scoring.model).modelId`, `resolvedModel` exported from `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts` (lifted from the equivalent guard already written, but kept private, in `src/lib/ai/tiers.test.ts:23-30`), never a name typed into the harness (AC-9, AC-11) |
| The JSON report's anchors field | whether the rubric text has moved since the data was authored | `bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS)`, a pure function in `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors-hash.ts` (sha256 over `BANDS.map(b => \`${b}:${BAND_ANCHORS[b]}\`).join("\n")`, first 12 hex characters), imported by both this report writer and the AC-10 test, so both read the one real function (AC-9) |
| The run's own exit code | pass, fail, aborted, or a mix | the aggregate of every pair's verdict, the preference leak flag, and whether the run aborted on a usage gate refusal (AC-7) |

**Key invariants**:
- A pair's five reruns are never fired concurrently with each other; only different pairs' test bodies may overlap (AC-2), bounded by `maxConcurrency` (Build plan, step 1).
- A verdict is never printed or reported without its denominator alongside it (AC-6).
- `pnpm eval` is never reachable from `pnpm test` or `pnpm test:integration`: it is its own Vitest project, selected only by explicit `--project eval` (which the `pnpm eval` script wraps), so no existing command starts spending real vendor calls by accident.
- Nothing under `test/eval/` or `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts` names a vendor package or a model id; every real call goes through `scoreListing()`, and the reported model id goes through the shared `resolvedModel()` guard (AC-11).
- The `BAND_ANCHORS` drift assertions (AC-10) live in the ordinary unit suite (`pnpm test`), never behind a vendor call, so a rubric edit is caught on every push, not only when someone happens to run the harness.
- The minted fixture user is deleted (`deleteFixtureUser`) after the report is written, in an `afterAll`, matching `test/helpers/fixture-user.ts`'s own reason for existing: an undeleted fixture user otherwise accumulates in the local database on every run, the same way `fit-scoring-live.test.ts` already avoids it. Cleanup runs after the report write, in that order, so a cleanup failure can never destroy the run's own output.
- One session is expected to outlive the whole run (sixteen pairs, bounded concurrency, five sequential calls each): this is assumed to comfortably fit inside Supabase's session lifetime today, and is not re verified per call. If feature 15's set grows large enough, or `ai_scoring` itself grows slower, to approach that lifetime, this assumption needs revisiting (Follow up).

**Security model**: No user facing surface and no user data. The fixture session this feature mints is the same development only, `DEV_SESSION_ENABLED` gated path `test/helpers/session.ts` and `test/helpers/fixture-user.ts` already use for `fit-scoring-live.test.ts`; nothing new is added to that gate. The one real exposure is that every archetype's `summary`, `skills`, and `experience` text reaches OpenAI on every run of this command, which is exactly spec 0016's own AC-1 (no real person, no real employer) doing its job here too.

**Configuration required**: none new. Reuses `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, and `DEV_SESSION_ENABLED`, already validated by `src/env.ts` and already required for the local Supabase stack this command needs running.

**Critical test scenarios**:
- Happy path: `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` scores that one pair for real, five sequential reruns under the one minted session, and prints a passing verdict with its denominator (e.g. "strong_match, 5 of 5 succeeded"), verifies **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-6**, **AC-9**.
- Failure case: a pair whose five reruns come back as 2 scored and 3 vendor failures is reported `inconclusive` (`insufficient-successes`) rather than a false pass or fail, the run's own exit code is non zero, and the other pairs in the same run still complete, verifies **AC-3**, **AC-7**.
- Abort case: constructed against `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts`'s own fixtures, the first rerun outcome carrying `allowed: false` (any `UsageGateReason`) stops the run from counting it toward any denominator and marks the run `aborted`, verifies **AC-3**.
- Data quality gate: `validateGroundTruth()` returning even one issue against a deliberately broken fixture set stops the command before any vendor call is made, verifies **AC-1**.
- Cross pair check: constructed verdicts where `preference-match` lands on `strong_match` but `preference-violation` lands on `good_match` (with `preference-title-conflict` unchanged) trip `preference-leak-suspected`, while all three landing together on `good_match` instead trips `baseline-drift`, verified against `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts`'s own fixtures rather than a real run, verifies **AC-5**.
- Drift guard: editing `BAND_ANCHORS`'s text fails the AC-10 test by name, under the ordinary free `pnpm test`, verifies **AC-10**.

## Build plan

This project's default build approach is Tracer Bullet (a thin end to end slice proven before scaling). Applied here: prove the whole real path, real vendor call, real verdict, real report, on exactly one pair before scaling to all sixteen and the cross pair and aggregate logic.

1. Add the `eval` Vitest project to `vitest.config.mts`: `extends: true` (pulls in the root `resolve.tsconfigPaths` and the `server-only` alias every other project already relies on; omitting it is exactly the failure Option 2 was rejected for, since `scoreListing()`'s own `import "server-only"` throws without it), `include: ["test/eval/**/*.test.ts"]`, `environment: "node"`, the shared `setupFiles`, `globalSetup: ["./test/setup/require-stack.ts"]`, `testTimeout: 300_000` (five sequential `ai_scoring` calls at its own 30 second `timeoutMs` ceiling each, plus headroom, since one pair's test body cannot finish faster than its slowest rerun), `hookTimeout: 60_000` (the fixture user mint against a possibly cold stack), `maxConcurrency: 4` (a real, installed Vitest 4.1.11 option bounding how many pairs' test bodies run at once; set explicitly rather than left at whatever the installed version currently defaults to), and `fileParallelism: false` scoped to this project alone, the same reason `integration-serial` already carries it: this project is written to hold exactly one file sharing one minted session and one report writer, and a second file here would run in a separate worker by Vitest's own default, mint a second session, and race the first on the same report filename. Add the `"eval": "vitest run --project eval"` script to `package.json`. Satisfies **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-11**.
2. Export `resolvedModel()` from `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts` (lifted from the equivalent already written, but currently private to `src/lib/ai/tiers.test.ts`, which switches to importing it instead of keeping its own copy), and add `bandAnchorsHash()` as a small pure function in `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors-hash.ts`. Write the pure verdict logic in `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts`: the three way outcome classification (refusal, rerun failure, scored success) from AC-3, the majority vote with the 3 of 5 inconclusive floor and the no majority/`acceptableBands` exception, the distinct `stability-probe` "every success inside `acceptableBands`" rule (AC-4), and the `preference-isolation` baseline comparison (AC-5). Wire `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts` against constructed fixtures for each rule, no vendor call involved. Satisfies **AC-3**, **AC-4**, **AC-5**, **AC-6**.
3. The thin thread: `test/eval/harness.test.ts`, one `describe("eval harness")`, a top level `beforeAll` running `validateGroundTruth()` (throwing with every issue if any, before anything else) then minting the one fixture session for the run; one `it.concurrent` per pair named `` `${pair.id} [${pair.tags.join(" ")}]` ``, whose body awaits five sequential `scoreListing()` calls, feeds the outcomes to step 2's verdict function, stores the result in a module scoped `Map<string, PairVerdict>` keyed by pair id, and asserts (via the test context's own `expect`, required under `it.concurrent`) that the verdict's status is `pass`, so `fail` and `inconclusive` both fail their own test with the denominator and distribution in the message; and a final `afterAll` that runs the preference leak check against the map, writes the JSON report (including the model id and anchors hash), then deletes the fixture user. Prove this against exactly `control-direct-match` (real vendor calls) before scaling: get `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` green end to end. Satisfies the first slice of **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-9**.
4. Scale to the full sixteen pairs, confirm `maxConcurrency` and `fileParallelism` behave as designed under a real, unfiltered `pnpm eval` run, and confirm the run's own exit code is non zero on a fail, an inconclusive pair, a leak, or an abort, and zero only when everything that ran passed cleanly. Satisfies the rest of **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-7**, **AC-8**.
5. Add the committed `BAND_ANCHORS` drift test under `src/features/scoring/eval/` (the ordinary unit project, no vendor call): a literal `toEqual` pin of today's text plus a `bandAnchorsHash()` equality check, both failing by name, pointing at spec 0016's dataset, the moment either changes. Satisfies **AC-10**.
6. Add `/test/eval/.output/` to `.gitignore`. Satisfies **AC-9**.

## Consequences

**Positive**:
- Spec 0015's AC-2 (do the five bands actually spread real listings) and spec 0016's whole purpose (a ground truth set with nothing to run it against) both get their first real answer.
- The preference isolation check gives a structural, named way to catch a preference leaking into the band, distinct from an equally real but different finding (the rubric drifting for everyone at once), which closes the gap `rubric.ts`'s own comment names as otherwise untestable.
- The `BAND_ANCHORS` drift test means a rubric wording change is caught by the free, always run unit suite, not only by someone remembering to run the paid harness and compare two reports by hand.
- Reusing `scoreListing()` unchanged, rather than a second call path straight to `TIERS`, means this feature can never drift from what the real app actually sends; a schema or prompt change is proven here exactly as it is proven in production. Aborting the whole run on the first usage gate refusal, rather than absorbing it into ordinary per pair accounting, keeps that same honesty: a budget or kill switch stop is reported as exactly what it is, not laundered into a wall of `inconclusive` verdicts that would misdescribe what actually happened.

**Negative / tradeoffs**:
- A full run spends 80 real vendor calls (16 pairs times 5 reruns) every time it runs the whole set; the `-t` subset filter is what keeps day to day iteration cheap, but this is still the largest deliberate, repeatable spend in this project, and it grows linearly with every future pair added to feature 15's set.
- The 3 of 5 success threshold for `inconclusive` means a genuinely bad but real result (all 5 reruns land on the same, wrong band) is never confused with a run too broken to trust, which is correct, but it also means an unlucky run (3 vendor timeouts and 2 real, matching answers) is reported exactly the same way as one with no useful data at all, even though 2 real matching answers is weak but real evidence. This spec accepts that loss rather than inventing a second, softer verdict tier.
- The preference leak check only covers the three pairs feature 15 built for exactly this purpose; it is not a general "did any preference move any band" detector across the other thirteen pairs, none of which vary a preference at all.
- `maxConcurrency` bounds how many pairs run at once, not how many vendor calls run at once across pairs; a pair whose own five reruns are mid flight does not free a concurrency slot until all five finish, so the actual number of simultaneous vendor calls can briefly exceed the pair level bound. This is accepted rather than built around, since the global day cap (1320) has wide headroom under this feature's whole weekly spend.
- Aborting the entire run on the first usage gate refusal means one unlucky global cap hit (shared with whatever else is calling `ai_scoring` at the time, including local `pnpm dev` usage) discards every result computed so far in that run, even pairs that had already cleanly passed. This is accepted because a refusal genuinely means the run's remaining data would not reflect real scoring anyway, not because the discarded cost is small.

**Neutral**:
- If the ground truth set (feature 15) grows past sixteen pairs, this feature's cost and run time grow with it; nothing here caps the set's size, that boundary belongs to spec 0016.
- The JSON report format is not versioned or schema checked; it is a plain, structural artifact for a human to read or diff by hand, not a contract another program depends on. If that changes later (a dashboard, a CI gate reading these reports), the format becomes its own decision.

## Follow-up

- [ ] This spec deliberately does not gate `pnpm eval` behind an explicit opt-in environment variable the way `TEST_LIVE_MODEL_CALLS_ENABLED` gates the one paid case inside `pnpm test:integration`. The safety mechanism here is that `eval` is its own Vitest project, reachable only by naming `--project eval` explicitly, and never included in `pnpm test` or `pnpm test:integration`. If a later command is ever added that runs every Vitest project unfiltered, revisit whether that alone is still enough.
- [ ] The global day cap for `ai_scoring` (1320, shared across everything that calls this tier, including local `pnpm dev` usage on `/search`, not scoped per fixture user) is the real ceiling this feature can hit, not the account weekly cap (500): since this feature mints a fresh fixture user every run, that account counter starts at zero each time and is not the binding constraint. Roughly sixteen full 80 call runs a day share that global ceiling with everything else touching `ai_scoring` locally; worth watching once this ships if iteration gets heavy, not solved here.
- [ ] `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts`'s `TIERS[tier].model` is typed `LanguageModel`, a union that also permits a plain gateway model id string `tiers.ts` itself never constructs; the `resolvedModel()` guard this feature exports narrows past that, matching the reasoning already written beside the guard it replaces in `tiers.test.ts`. If `tiers.ts` ever legitimately needs the string form, `resolvedModel()`'s own throw is where that would first surface, and it would need revisiting then, not guessed at now.
- [x] Root `AGENTS.md`'s `## Commands` section (line 37) still describes Vitest as "two projects"; it was already stale before this feature (spec 0011 added the third, `integration-serial`, on 2026-09-03) and this feature adds a fourth plus a new `pnpm eval` script the commands list does not yet name. `/architect` does not edit `AGENTS.md`; flagging it here for `/sync` or a direct edit once this feature builds. **Done 2026-09-08 at feature close**, by direct edit, the option this item itself names. The claim was verified first and was accurate on both counts. The section now names all four projects with the spec that added each, and the commands block carries `pnpm eval` marked as paid, together with the fact that the binding ceiling is the shared `ai_scoring` global day cap rather than the account weekly cap, since the harness mints a fresh fixture user every run.
- [ ] This spec assumes the one minted session comfortably outlives a full run (sixteen pairs, bounded concurrency, five sequential calls each) without needing a refresh. If feature 15's set grows large enough, or a slower model tier is ever routed through this same harness, to make that assumption doubtful, re minting per pair (at the cost of more setup calls) is the fix, not something this build needs to solve preemptively.

1	# 0016. Eval ground truth set
2	
3	**Date**: 2026-09-07
4	**Status**: Accepted
5	
6	## Summary
7	
8	This spec defines the authored data feature 16's eval harness will run against: four invented candidate profiles (never a real person's data) and sixteen fixed pairs of one profile against one job posting, each with a band decided from the rubric's own written wording before any model is asked. It fixes a real gap in an earlier draft: the draft assumed the rubric caps a candidate's band by seniority, and that rule is not actually written anywhere in `rubric.ts`. Where the rubric's wording genuinely cannot settle one exact band on its own, the pair carries a range of acceptable bands instead of a single invented answer, and the gap is handed to spec 0015 to consider closing later.
9	
10	## Context
11	
12	See [rationale.md](rationale.md) for the full problem context: why a ground truth set is needed at all, the options weighed for this pair set's shape, and the rejected paths.
13	
14	## Requirements
15	
16	**User stories**:
17	- As the person maintaining the scoring rubric, I want a fixed set of profile and posting pairs with a band decided in advance, so a later prompt or model change can be checked against real expectations instead of a fresh read of the output.
18	- As the person running feature 16's harness, I want to know which pairs allow more than one acceptable band, so a run does not report a genuine rubric ambiguity as a scoring bug.
19	- As the person maintaining spec 0015's rubric, I want any gap the ground truth set finds in the anchor wording written down plainly, so it can be closed on purpose rather than guessed at again later.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria**:
22	- **AC-1**: `src/features/scoring/eval/archetypes.ts` defines at least four candidate archetypes. Each is a fully invented person: no real name, no real employer, no text traced back to any real person's history. Each clears spec 0015's AC-7 scoring gate (at least one skill or one work history entry). Each represents a plainly different career shape from the others (documented in a short `description` field, separate from the `summary` text actually sent to the model).
23	- **AC-2**: Across the full pair set, every one of the five bands (`strong_match`, `good_match`, `possible_match`, `weak_match`, `not_a_match`) appears as the `expectedBand` or inside the `acceptableBands` of at least one pair. Wherever `rubric.ts`'s written anchor text alone can support one confident answer, the pair states a single exact `expectedBand`, not a range.
24	- **AC-3**: At least one pair is built specifically around a severe experience or seniority shortfall paired with a genuinely overlapping named skill. Because `BAND_ANCHORS` (`rubric.ts:69`) names a seniority expectation only inside `strong_match` and states nothing about how a severe shortfall elsewhere should weigh against one overlapping skill, this pair's `acceptableBands` holds more than one band rather than asserting a single invented answer, and its `rationale` field states the ambiguity plainly and points at spec 0015 as the place to resolve it.
25	- **AC-4**: At least three pairs share one archetype and near identical posting skill and experience requirements, differing only in whether the posting conflicts with that archetype's own `preferences` (which the prompt does send, `rubric.ts:437-463`). Between them they cover all four preference dimensions spec 0015's Follow up names, **title, location, remote, and pay**: the stated title against `desired_titles`, the stated location against `desired_locations`, the on site or remote language against `remote_preference`, and the pay figure against `minimum_pay`. Every conflict is written into `title`, `location` or `descriptionSnippet` (three of the four fields `buildScoringPrompt` sends, alongside `companyName`; salary fields are never sent, so the pay conflict has to live in `descriptionSnippet`'s text, never in `salaryMin`/`salaryMax`). Every one of these pairs carries the same `expectedBand`. A harness run scoring them differently is evidence that a stated preference moved the band, which spec 0015's own instructions forbid.
26	
27	  **Grouped by what a preference describes, not one pair per dimension.** This is a decision, not an accident of how the set grew, and it is what the third pair's existence turns on. Two reasons put title in its own pair and leave the other three together:
28	
29	  - **Coverage.** Title was the dimension covered nowhere. Before this amendment the set already varied location, remote and pay together in `preference-violation`, so all three had a case that could catch them leaking; title had none, and no pair anywhere in the set conflicted with `desired_titles` while holding skills fixed. Title needed a pair of its own for that reason alone. Location did not, because it already had one.
30	  - **Semantic fusion.** A title names the work itself. A fit judgment about a Backend Engineer posting and a stated desire for a Backend Engineer title are one short step apart, which makes the two easy to fuse even for a model following the instruction in good faith. Location, remote and pay describe the circumstances of employment and are orthogonal to capability, so reading any of them as a fit signal takes a longer and less natural step. Title is the likeliest leak, so it gets the pair that can name it unambiguously.
31	
32	  Those three stay together because they share one failure mode, the model reading stated circumstances as a fit signal, and because splitting them would add two vendor calls to every harness run forever to buy a diagnosis that bisecting once gives for free.
33	
34	  **The reasoning this replaced, recorded so it is not reintroduced.** An earlier draft of this clause argued that title is the only preference whose value has a structured counterpart among the fields `buildScoringPrompt` sends. That is false. The prompt sends `Title:`, `Company:` and `Location:` for the posting and `- Desired titles:`, `- Desired locations:`, `- Remote preference:` and `- Minimum pay:` for the candidate (`rubric.ts:451-479`), so `Location:` against `- Desired locations:` is the same structure as `Title:` against `- Desired titles:`; this spec's own `preference-violation` pair puts `Location: Chicago, IL` and `- Desired locations: Atlanta, GA, Remote` in one prompt. Remote and pay are the two with no structured counterpart, reaching the model only as description prose. Applied honestly that rule would isolate location too, which the cost argument above argues against, so the rule was wrong rather than merely imprecisely worded.
35	
36	  A fifth preference dimension, if one is ever added to the profile feature, is placed by asking what it describes: **the work itself, or the circumstances around it.** One that describes the work joins title and earns its own pair, because that is where fusion with a fit judgment is plausible. One that describes circumstances joins the grouped pair. Do not decide it by asking whether the value has a counterpart among the listing fields; that test does not separate these four.
37	- **AC-5**: At least one pair is tagged `stability-probe`: a posting whose `descriptionSnippet` states no concrete requirement, skill, or seniority language at all, authored close to the 500 character Adzuna ceiling (not a short snippet with a decorative ellipsis appended), and ending in the literal ellipsis character U+2026, the exact character `buildScoringPrompt`'s own check reads (`descriptionSnippet.trimEnd().endsWith("…")`, `rubric.ts:490`) to route a listing into its cut off branch. The near full length matters as much as the character itself: only then is `buildScoringPrompt`'s own claim, "this is the first 500 characters of a longer description", actually true of this fixture, rather than a mismatch between what the prompt asserts and what the snippet really contains. Its data records the real instability spec 0015's Follow up already observed for this exact input shape (the same excerpt scoring `strong_match` three times and `possible_match` six times in one 2026-09-06 render) rather than asserting one confident band. `validateGroundTruth()` checks that every `stability-probe` tagged pair's `descriptionSnippet` ends in U+2026, since a plain three period `...` would silently land the pair in the untruncated branch and defeat the point of the pair.
38	- **AC-6**: Every archetype's `profile` field is exactly a `ScoringProfile` (`src/features/scoring/rubric.ts:259`). Every pair's `listing` field is exactly a `Listing` (`src/features/search/adzuna.ts:162`), authored as frozen literal text, never a live Adzuna fetch, with `descriptionSnippet` never exceeding the 500 character `ADZUNA_SNIPPET_CHARACTERS` ceiling `rubric.ts` already names.
39	- **AC-7**: The archetypes and pairs live as typed TypeScript modules under `src/features/scoring/eval/`, not inside a `.test.ts` file and not embedded in feature 16's own harness code, so a malformed entry is a compile error against the app's own `ScoringProfile`, `Listing`, and `Band` types rather than a runtime surprise.
40	- **AC-8**: A pure `validateGroundTruth()` function catches what TypeScript's structural typing cannot: a duplicate id, a pair whose `archetypeId` names no real archetype, a band missing from every pair's `expectedBand` and `acceptableBands`, a `descriptionSnippet` longer than 500 characters, an `acceptableBands` that omits its own `expectedBand` or holds fewer than two bands, a `stability-probe` tagged pair whose `descriptionSnippet` does not end in the literal U+2026 character, and the absence of a `preference-isolation` or `stability-probe` tagged pair. Each returned issue names which check failed and which id, band, or tag triggered it (the `GroundTruthIssue` shape below). A committed guard test asserts it returns no issues for the current, real data, and separately asserts, against deliberately malformed inline fixtures, that each of these checks actually fires on its own broken case, not only that the real data happens to pass. Running under `pnpm test`, so an edit that silently narrows the set, or a validator that silently stops checking something, both fail the unit suite.
41	
42	## Options considered
43	
44	See [rationale.md](rationale.md).
45	
46	## Decision
47	
48	**Chosen option**: Option 2, four fully fictional archetypes with every expected band traced to the rubric's own written text, and a widened tolerance for the one case that text cannot settle alone (rationale.md has the full comparison against reusing the earlier three archetype draft as is, and against blocking this feature on a spec 0015 amendment first).
49	
50	## Rationale
51	
52	Full reasoning and the rejected options: see [rationale.md](rationale.md).

138	| id | Archetype | Posting brief | `expectedBand` | `acceptableBands` | Tags | Why |
139	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
